 A unit test should generally be:

Given these preconditions (in `let`, `before`, or `around` blocks)
When I call this production code (one action or sequence of actions in the `it` test block)
Then I see this behavior (one assertion as the last line of the `it` test block)

For feature tests, this is generally acceptable and preferable for me:

Given these preconditions
When I do these things
Then I see this output
When I do this additional thing
Then I see this additional thing
And I see this other thing

This distinction of what's acceptable/preferred is made for two reasons: first, feature tests often require a back-and-forth flow of actions across the application... doing things and asserting the outcomes. Limiting this as much as possible is good, but not at the expense of making the set of actions and all the expectations of behavior isolated from each other. For example, if saving a form should result in both a confirmation message and a redirect to show the data, then having both expectations in the same test ties the flow of those things together and more succinctly & completely describes the user's experience. Secondly, pragmatically because browser tests are slower, running the same action in multiple tests to assert different things will slow down the test suite more quickly over time.
